request.description:
Requires the `update` action on `/system/weapons`.

**Every field is optional and an absent one is left alone.** `targets` and `allowances` are
arrays, and an explicit `[]` CLEARS them — which is why they are not simply omitted when
unchanged: only a pointer can tell "not mentioned" from "set to empty".

**To clear `code`, send an empty string.** The column is nullable and refuses a blank one, so
there is exactly one representation of "no code" and an empty string is folded into it. `null`
cannot be used to clear anything — see the note on PATCH and nullable fields at the top of this
document.

**The `weapon` object is REPLACED AS A UNIT, not merged field by field.** Its fields are one set
of figures measured together: a merge would let a request change the range while silently
keeping the loadout recorded for the old one. A client editing one figure sends the object
whole, and the fields it omits within that object are cleared to unknown.

**`kind` is not writable.** It is the route the caller used, so changing it would move a row
between catalogues while the URL still named the old one. A weapon id sent to `/mines/{id}` is
`400` naming both kinds rather than a `404` — the id is valid and the collection is wrong.

**The picture is REPLACED when the request carries a `file` part, and left alone when it does not.**
`DELETE /weapons/{id}/image` is what removes one.

keeping those. A picker for a hull's own loadout is the ACTUAL leg, which is not modelled yet

request.description:
Requires the `read` action on `/system/weapons`.

**The kind is in the PATH and is not a query parameter.** `/weapons` cannot be asked for
sensors, so there is no second way to state which catalogue is meant and therefore no way for
the two to disagree.

**`search` matches the name, the tactical code AND the capability text**, because the design's
own box claims to — *"Cari nama senjata atau kemampuan..."*. A name-only search would miss a
weapon whose capability is the only place a word appears.

**`id_sensor_category` is REFUSED with `400` here, not ignored.** The category filter exists on
the sensor tab alone, so a request that sends one to `/weapons` is a client bug — and a
parameter accepted and quietly ignored would tell the caller their filter worked.

Rows carry their targets and their allowances. A weapon's figures are nested under `weapon`; the
`mine` and `sensor` objects are **absent**, not null.

formdata.description:
The fields, as a JSON document — the schema is
`#/components/schemas/EquipmentCreateRequest`.

The picture. PNG or JPEG, at most 5 MiB. Omit it to create the row with no picture.

A file that cannot be decoded as one of those is **`400` naming `file`** — never a field
of the row, because the operator sent a file and the message should name what they sent.

request.description:
Requires the `create` action on `/system/weapons`.

**The `weapon` object is required and the other two must be absent.** Sending `mine` to this
path is `400` naming `mine`, and sending two of the three is `400` as well — the row has one set
of figures and the path has already said which.

**`code` is unique among live rows ACROSS ALL THREE CATALOGUES**, not within this one. That is
the reason weapons, mines and sensors share one table at all: PostgreSQL has no cross-table
unique constraint, so three tables could not have prevented `WPN-001` existing as both a weapon
and a mine. A clash is `409` with `data.errors.code`.

**`name` is likewise unique among live rows, case-insensitively**, and a clash is `409` with
`data.errors.name`. Both indexes are **partial on `deleted_at IS NULL`**, so retiring a row
releases its name and code for reuse.

**Lookup ids are validated before the foreign key sees them.** An unknown `id_weapon_kind` is
`400` with `data.errors["weapon.id_weapon_kind"]` rather than a constraint violation naming no
field — the contract elsewhere says these ids come from `/helpers` and are never hardcoded, so a
client that guessed is making the common mistake.

**`level` NAMES ONE OF FOUR SUBJECTS: `unit`, `class`, `type` or `category`.** Anything else is refused
by VALIDATION — `400` with the error under **`level`** and the message "This field must be one of unit class
type category." — so a request carrying one never reaches a handler.

**ALL FOUR ARE WRITABLE AGAIN AS OF 2026-10-13.** Between 2026-10-12 and that day only the three
inherited levels were accepted, because a hull's own declaration had a route of its own that existed to
carry a per-hull NUMBER. B56 removed the number, that route went with it, and this body is once more the
one place all four levels are authored.

**AN ARRAY OF OBJECTS REPORTS ITS FIELDS WITHOUT A PATH.** `level` above, not `allowances[0].level`: the
binder flattens a nested struct element's field name. An array of SCALARS is indexed by contrast — a bad
`targets` entry is `data.errors["targets[1]"]`. Both come from validation, not from a handler, and this
note exists because the two shapes disagree.

**A subject must be a live row at the level it names.** A retired class, type or category is
refused with `400` naming `allowances[i].id_level` — the INDEX is in the field name because a list
of level-bearing declarations has no single field to give. Declaring the same subject twice is
`400` naming the second of the pair.

**`422` IS NOT POSSIBLE HERE, and that follows from the media type rather than from this
operation.** On a JSON body, a field of the wrong TYPE is `422` naming `_request`: the body could not
be read, and there is no field to name. On a MULTIPART request the fields arrive as a `payload`
STRING, so the same mistake is a **`400` naming `payload`** — the part was read, and what failed was
parsing it. Malformed JSON inside the part gets the same answer for the same reason.

A `400` naming an ordinary field therefore means the payload PARSED and a rule was broken — and for
an array element it names the position, as in `data.errors["targets[1]"]`.

The response is the STORED row, read back through the same path as the list, so it carries the
subjects' names and the presigned `image_url`. A client can append it to the page it is showing
without a follow-up call.

**A picture may be attached to this same request**, in the optional `file` part — see the request
body. Omit it and the row is created with no photograph, which is the ordinary case for a catalogue
still being filled in. Remove one with `DELETE /weapons/{id}/image`.

item.name: What one hull really carries from the mine catalogue

query.description:
The hull whose OWN allowances are being read or replaced.

**A SECOND DECLARATION OF THE SAME QUERY PARAMETER, because the OPTIONALITY differs and OpenAPI 3.0
states `required` on the parameter itself rather than at the point of use.** `ForUnit` above is the
same `for_unit` used as a FILTER on a catalogue list, where its absence is the ordinary "show me
everything"; these routes have no such reading, so theirs is required. One object cannot be both, and
the wire name is identical — both declare `name: for_unit`.

**REQUIRED ON THESE ROUTES, AND OPTIONAL ON THE CATALOGUE LIST.** The same parameter both places, with
the opposite optionality, because the role differs: on a catalogue list it NARROWS a collection the caller
could read anyway, so its absence is the ordinary "show me everything"; here it names the SUBJECT, so its
absence leaves the route with nothing to describe.

An id that is not a live hull is a **400 naming this field** — not an empty list, which would say
"this hull may be given nothing" about a hull that does not exist.

query.description:
Rows per page. Optional here with a default of 25, which means
`pagination.PaginationFilter` must relax its current `required` validation to
match — as written, omitting it is a 400.

Narrows the catalogue to what ONE HULL may be given, and answers each row's governing declaration in
`allowance`.

**THE LADDER IS RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE**: the nearest declaration wins — the hull's own, then its
class, then its type, then its category. A hull that inherits its allowance from its class gets
`level: "class"` with the class's id, so a screen can say WHERE a figure came from rather than
showing a number the operator cannot check.

**EVERY RETURNED ROW IS ONE A DECLARATION REACHES** — the hull's own, or one inherited from its
class, type or category — so this read IS the criteria seen from one hull: lower a declaration and
the number on the row follows it, remove one and the row leaves the list when nothing else governs
it. That is what makes it a different thing from `GET /units/{id}/embarkation-candidates`, which
instantiates a rule into concrete hulls to **attach** and carries no number at all, the complements
keeping those. A picker for a hull's own loadout is the ACTUAL leg, which is not modelled yet
(`docs/backlog.md` B55).

**IT IS A FILTER ON THE CATALOGUE RATHER THAN A ROUTE UNDER `/units`, DELIBERATELY.** Each catalogue
has its own permission, so a caller here sees exactly the catalogues they may already read; a route
under `/units` could only be gated on the unit register, and that would hand a Referee trusted with
the sensor list the whole weaponry.

**AN ID THAT IS NOT A LIVE HULL IS `400` NAMING `for_unit`**, not an empty page — an empty
catalogue reads as "this hull may be given nothing", a far more alarming answer than "no such
hull".
Matches the name, the code and the capability text, case-insensitively.

**Refused on this catalogue.** `/weapons` and `/mines` answer `400` for it; only `/sensors`
accepts it.

search rules. `id_sensor_category` is **refused here too** — the category filter is the sensor
tab's alone.

`level: "class"` with the class's id, so a screen can say WHERE a figure came from rather than
showing a number the operator cannot check.

**EVERY RETURNED ROW IS ONE A DECLARATION REACHES** — the hull's own, or one inherited from its
class, type or category — so this read IS the criteria seen from one hull: lower a declaration and
the number on the row follows it, remove one and the row leaves the list when nothing else governs
it. That is what makes it a different thing from `GET /units/{id}/embarkation-candidates`, which
instantiates a rule into concrete hulls to **attach** and carries no number at all, the complements
keeping those. A picker for a hull's own loadout is the ACTUAL leg, which is not modelled yet
(`docs/backlog.md` B55).

**IT IS A FILTER ON THE CATALOGUE RATHER THAN A ROUTE UNDER `/units`, DELIBERATELY.** Each catalogue
has its own permission, so a caller here sees exactly the catalogues they may already read; a route
under `/units` could only be gated on the unit register, and that would hand a Referee trusted with
the sensor list the whole weaponry.

**AN ID THAT IS NOT A LIVE HULL IS `400` NAMING `for_unit`**, not an empty page — an empty
catalogue reads as "this hull may be given nothing", a far more alarming answer than "no such
hull".
Matches the name, the code and the capability text, case-insensitively.

**Refused on this catalogue.** `/weapons` and `/mines` answer `400` for it; only `/sensors`
accepts it.

query.description:
The hull whose OWN allowances are being read or replaced.

**A SECOND DECLARATION OF THE SAME QUERY PARAMETER, because the OPTIONALITY differs and OpenAPI 3.0
states `required` on the parameter itself rather than at the point of use.** `ForUnit` above is the
same `for_unit` used as a FILTER on a catalogue list, where its absence is the ordinary "show me
everything"; these routes have no such reading, so theirs is required. One object cannot be both, and
the wire name is identical — both declare `name: for_unit`.

**REQUIRED ON THESE ROUTES, AND OPTIONAL ON THE CATALOGUE LIST.** The same parameter both places, with
the opposite optionality, because the role differs: on a catalogue list it NARROWS a collection the caller
could read anyway, so its absence is the ordinary "show me everything"; here it names the SUBJECT, so its
absence leaves the route with nothing to describe.

An id that is not a live hull is a **400 naming this field** — not an empty list, which would say
"this hull may be given nothing" about a hull that does not exist.

request.description:
Requires the `update` action on `/system/sensors`.

Every field is optional and an absent one is left alone; an explicit `[]` clears `targets` or
`allowances`; an empty `code` clears the code. The `sensor` object, when sent, **replaces the
figures as a unit** — so a request that changes only the range must still send `emits`, or the
flag falls back to `false`.

A sensor id sent to `/weapons/{id}` or `/mines/{id}` is `400` naming both kinds.

query.description:
Rows per page. Optional here with a default of 25, which means
`pagination.PaginationFilter` must relax its current `required` validation to
match — as written, omitting it is a 400.

Narrows the catalogue to what ONE HULL may be given, and answers each row's governing declaration in
`allowance`.

**THE LADDER IS RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE**: the nearest declaration wins — the hull's own, then its
class, then its type, then its category. A hull that inherits its allowance from its class gets
`level: "class"` with the class's id, so a screen can say WHERE a figure came from rather than
showing a number the operator cannot check.

**EVERY RETURNED ROW IS ONE A DECLARATION REACHES** — the hull's own, or one inherited from its
class, type or category — so this read IS the criteria seen from one hull: lower a declaration and
the number on the row follows it, remove one and the row leaves the list when nothing else governs
it. That is what makes it a different thing from `GET /units/{id}/embarkation-candidates`, which
instantiates a rule into concrete hulls to **attach** and carries no number at all, the complements
keeping those. A picker for a hull's own loadout is the ACTUAL leg, which is not modelled yet
(`docs/backlog.md` B55).

**IT IS A FILTER ON THE CATALOGUE RATHER THAN A ROUTE UNDER `/units`, DELIBERATELY.** Each catalogue
has its own permission, so a caller here sees exactly the catalogues they may already read; a route
under `/units` could only be gated on the unit register, and that would hand a Referee trusted with
the sensor list the whole weaponry.

**AN ID THAT IS NOT A LIVE HULL IS `400` NAMING `for_unit`**, not an empty page — an empty
catalogue reads as "this hull may be given nothing", a far more alarming answer than "no such
hull".
Matches the name, the code and the capability text, case-insensitively.

The sensor tab's own filter, from `/helpers` under `sensor_categories`. **Accepted only on
this catalogue** — `/weapons` and `/mines` answer `400` for it rather than ignoring it.

request.description:
Requires the `read` action on `/system/sensors`.

**THE ONE CATALOGUE THAT ACCEPTS `id_sensor_category`.** The design puts a category filter on the
sensor tab and nowhere else, and an id that matches no sensor returns an empty page rather than
a `404` — the vocabulary is read from `/helpers` under `sensor_categories`.

Rows carry their category, their platform and whether they emit. See `GET /weapons` for the
search rules.

response.name: One page of the sensor catalogue.

formdata.description:
The fields, as a JSON document — the schema is
`#/components/schemas/EquipmentCreateRequest`.

The picture. PNG or JPEG, at most 5 MiB. Omit it to create the row with no picture.

A file that cannot be decoded as one of those is **`400` naming `file`** — never a field
of the row, because the operator sent a file and the message should name what they sent.

request.description:
Requires the `create` action on `/system/sensors`.

**`id_sensor_category` and `id_sensor_platform` are both required inside the `sensor` object**,
from `/helpers` under `sensor_categories` and `sensor_platforms`. An unknown id is `400` naming
the field — `sensor.id_sensor_category` or `sensor.id_sensor_platform` — rather than a
constraint violation naming nothing.

**`emits` defaults to `false`**, because the column is NOT NULL and an absent field writes the
zero value. That is the safer silent assumption: a passive set is what an operator who did not
say gets, rather than a radar nobody recorded.

request.description:
**THE CODE IS SHARED BY EVERY GAME ON THE MISSION**, so this changes what several exercises display
